newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's SRC to shut 14,000-bpd hydrocracker.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's SRC to shut 14,000-bpd hydrocracker.

text.p: Singapore Refining Capacity Co (SRC) willl carry out an unscheduled shutdown of a 14,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) hydrocracker No. 2 mid-February for 10-14 days, a company source said on Monday.
The source said the unit, which produces mainly kerosene and diesel, will be shut down due to a pressure build-up.
SRC has scheduled a shutdown of its 18,000-bpd hydrocracker No. 1 during the turnaround of its 90,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) No.1 from March 2-22, the source said.
He said during the same period, a 18 million cubic feet per day hydrogen plant will be down for statutory inspection.
A 32,000-bpd visbreaker will also be shut from March 4-17 to tie-in with CDU No.2. Runs at the 135,000-bpd CDU may be marginally reduced during this time, the source said.

SRC is 40-percent owned by Singapore Petroleum Co. The remaining stake in the company is shared between British Petroleum & Co Plc and Caltex Group of Companies. Caltex is a joint-venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc .
